The belief: one state class with
fields is the simplest safe way to model a screen. It's one class with one
, and every widget can read every field.

The first half is true. The Bloc library's own guide lists this approach as "Simple" and "Concise", and it's a shape most developers have written many times. It also has a real strength: states that overlap, such as showing an error snackbar while the old data stays on screen, fit naturally. The trouble is the word "safe". The same guide's first con is "Not Type Safe", and it warns that "it's possible to emit a malformed state which can lead to bugs."

blocks.title: Let the requirement pick the model

content.text: The Bloc guide sums up the trade-off: sealed classes work best "for well-defined, exclusive states with unique properties", while a single class with a status enum works best "for simple states or when the requirements call for states that aren't exclusive".
